cases.name: Ada C. Bradbury Bean
cases.about: She was a widow, and at one time worked as a research secretary at Harvard University, and was a secretary at Associated Business Machines. Neighbors described Mrs. Bean as a petite, attractive woman, quiet and pleasant. There was reportedly blood splattered everywhere, even on the ceiling.
cases.narrative: On 2/6/1969, during a welfare check she was found on her bed, face down, her nightclothes pulled over her head, covered by blankets.

cases.name: Jane Britton
cases.about: She was described as a smart and funny and was a graduate student in Near Eastern archaeology at Harvard University.
cases.caseStatus: CODIS / DNA MATCH; COLD CASE SOLVED; FORENSIC INVESTIGATIVE GENETIC GENEALOGY SOLVED; SUSPECT DECEASED WHEN ID'D
cases.narrative: On 1/8/1969, her boyfriend went to her apartment and found her body face down on her bed with her nightgown pulled over her head. She had multiple lacerations to her head with underlying skull fractures, as well as a bruise on her arm. Police speculated that a 4-by-6-inch stone with a pointed end, a souvenir Britton had brought home from an Iranian dig, had been used. It was missing, and the state police found no weapon in the apartment.
